name: Diffuse Alveolar Hemorrhage Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of hemoptysis or blood-stained sputum
Diffuse bilateral alveolar infiltrates on chest imaging
Bronchoalveolar lavage showing progressively bloodier aliquots or hemosiderin-laden macrophages
New onset or worsening anemia without other obvious source of bleeding
Exclusion of other causes of pulmonary infiltrates and bleeding such as infection or trauma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Diffuse bilateral alveolar infiltrates on imaging plus bronchoalveolar lavage demonstrating alveolar hemorrhage, with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Hemoptysis may be absent in up to one-third of cases; diagnosis relies heavily on imaging and lavage findings.

pathognomonic.notes: Coughing up blood is a key clinical feature but may be absent in some cases
Radiologic hallmark on chest X-ray or CT
Severe impairment of gas exchange due to alveolar filling

common.notes: Shortness of breath due to impaired oxygenation
Due to blood loss into alveoli
May be present if underlying inflammatory or autoimmune cause

occasional.notes: Dry or productive cough may occur
Chronic cases or underlying systemic disease
May indicate underlying vasculitis or autoimmune disorder
Suggests associated renal involvement in systemic vasculitis
May be present in systemic autoimmune diseases

rare.notes: Rarely associated with systemic vasculitis affecting CNS

laboratory: Decreased hemoglobin and hematocrit consistent with anemia
Presence of hemosiderin-laden macrophages in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid
Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) in autoimmune cases
Possible positive autoimmune serologies (ANCA, anti-GBM antibodies)
imaging: Diffuse bilateral alveolar infiltrates on chest X-ray
Ground-glass opacities and consolidation on chest CT scan
genetic: No specific genetic markers; may be associated with HLA subtypes in autoimmune etiologies
other: Bronchoscopy with progressively bloodier lavage aliquots
Pulmonary function tests showing restrictive pattern and decreased diffusing capacity

distinguishingFeatures: Systemic vasculitis signs such as skin rash, neuropathy
Sudden onset dyspnea and chest pain
Absence of alveolar hemorrhage on lavage

redFlags: New or worsening anemia without external bleeding source
references: Jennette JC, et al. 2013. 2012 Revised International Chapel Hill Consensus Conference Nomenclature of Vasculitides. Arthritis Rheum.
Collard HR, Schwarz MI. Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage. Clin Chest Med. 2004.
Sethi S, et al. Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage: a clinical review. Chest. 2020.
